quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A dirt or gravel road
A strip of oil in the center of a lane
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers are all slippery. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will come on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast causes your motorcycle to lurch forward and the rear tire to skid. This causes you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What is a benefit of checking your motorcycle thoroughly?

options.text: It is only useful if a mechanic does it.
It should not be done before a ride.
It should only be done after a ride.
It can find mechanical problems or broken equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can find mechanical problems or broken equipment.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if a hazard appears.
It makes it easier for you to communicate.
It makes it easier for other vehicles to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if a hazard appears.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. Riding side by side limits both riders' options if a hazard appears.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve OPEN, not closed.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time while riding?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready over the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time needed to react to hazards.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms should hold you up on the seat.
You can easily reach all the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach all the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips, not stretched. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: How should you ride at night compared to riding during the day?

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
Ride at the same speed as you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.
Ride on the shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day under the same conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead of you.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start slowing earlier, and increase your following distance.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your riding?

options.text: Well below the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use headlights from other vehicles to help you see.
Make yourself visible.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam, use other vehicles' headlights to see, and wear reflective gear. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and maintain safe space.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Front and emergency
Rear and emergency
Front and rear
Only a front brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: You lose grip with one or both wheels.
You stop before you expect to.
You get a flat tire.
You take too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose grip with one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Over-braking can cause you to lose traction and crash.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as visible as a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when you slow down quickly so others notice you.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that reduces your space cushion and helps others see you.
One that increases your space cushion and helps others see you.
One that puts you near road hazards and lets others pass you.
One that keeps you near road hazards and close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space cushion and helps others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion and lets others see you. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: They see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting how far you ride in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Wear clothing to protect yourself from the elements. Avoid artificial stimulants because they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handle grips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep going straight. Gradually brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Passing on a motorcycle is similar to passing in a car, but what is different?

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle than in a car. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into a driver's blind spot. Drivers may also fail to notice you even when they are looking.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Tighten your grip on the handle grips and speed up.
Travel in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to compensate is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never
Only during the day
Only at night
Day and night

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to increase how visible you are.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane
In any portion of the lane
On the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane because it is not your responsibility.
Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp if possible.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave within your lane to be more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If another lane is not available, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what is usually safest?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks that cross at an angle, cross them while riding straight within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.
